subject.title: Nix: speed up gateway builds and enforce cache-only CI consumers

question: Should maintainers close this stale branch as superseded, or port only the remaining source-builder move optimization onto current main?
rationale: Current main already absorbed the safety pieces and later changed the source-builder install model, so automation should not choose whether the old `mv` behavior still belongs in the package contract.

options.title: Close as superseded
options.body: Treat current main's npm-default gateway path, smoke checks, retained `dontFixup`, and symlink validation as the accepted resolution, and close this stale branch manually.

options.title: Port only the move optimization
options.body: Rebase a tiny source-builder patch that preserves `dist-runtime`, plugin manifests, bundled skills/templates, cleanup, wrapper defaults, and package gates while changing only the still-wanted copy/move behavior.

recommendation.title: Close as superseded
recommendation.body: Treat current main's npm-default gateway path, smoke checks, retained `dontFixup`, and symlink validation as the accepted resolution, and close this stale branch manually.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the branch trim and the later current-main gateway packaging changes that determine whether this old optimization still fits.
